hero.eyebrow: WHO World Malaria Report 2024 · IHME GBD · RBM Partnership
hero.description: Global malaria cases, deaths, at-risk populations, country burden rankings, insecticide resistance, and progress toward malaria elimination targets.

trends.note: Cases rose sharply during COVID-19 disruption of health services. Decline in 2025 reflects expanded vaccine rollout.

riskFactors.title: Young Children (Under 5)
riskFactors.description: Children under 5 account for 76% of all malaria deaths due to lack of acquired immunity. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the greatest burden.

riskFactors.title: Insecticide Resistance
riskFactors.description: Resistance to pyrethroid insecticides — used in bed nets — is now detected in 78 countries, directly threatening vector control programs.

riskFactors.title: Pregnant Women
riskFactors.description: Malaria in pregnancy causes maternal anaemia, low birth weight and neonatal mortality in high-transmission areas.

riskFactors.title: Climate Change
riskFactors.description: Rising temperatures are expanding mosquito habitats into higher altitudes and latitudes, increasing at-risk populations globally.

riskFactors.title: Artemisinin Resistance
riskFactors.description: Partial artemisinin resistance has been confirmed in 6 African countries, threatening the efficacy of first-line combination treatments.

didYouKnow: The RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) vaccine was approved by WHO in 2021 — the world's first malaria vaccine to reach approval.
A child dies from malaria approximately every 70 seconds in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Malaria costs Africa an estimated $12 billion in lost GDP annually through illness and premature death.
Malaria was responsible for more deaths than COVID-19 in Sub-Saharan Africa during 2020–2021.

faq.q: Is there a vaccine for malaria?
faq.a: Yes. The RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) vaccine and the R21/Matrix-M vaccine are both WHO-recommended for children in sub-Saharan Africa as of 2023. They provide partial protection and are used alongside other preventive measures.

faq.q: Which countries have the highest malaria burden?
faq.a: Nigeria, DR Congo, Uganda, Mozambique, and Côte d'Ivoire together account for over 50% of all global malaria cases. All five countries are in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Yes. Over 40 countries have successfully eliminated malaria. The WHO Global Malaria Strategy 2016–2030 aims for a 90% reduction in cases and deaths by 2030 compared to 2015 levels.
